scout.purpose: Cancellation prevents obsolete work from consuming resources or publishing stale results, but it only works when code cooperates and cleanup preserves the cancellation signal.
scout.realWorldUse: Search replacement, navigation, network calls, parsing, loops, locks, and resource use all encounter normal cancellation.
scout.outcome: Write cancellation-cooperative code, apply timeouts at the correct boundary, and perform non-cancellable cleanup only when essential.

sections.title: Cancellation is a normal control signal

blocks.text: Cancelling a Job requests cancellation and normally causes suspending functions to throw CancellationException. It propagates down the job tree and should propagate back out, not become a generic failure banner. Search flatMapLatest, a changed screen, or a timeout may cancel healthy but obsolete work. catch blocks that handle Exception must rethrow CancellationException or use APIs whose contracts preserve it. finally executes for cleanup as the coroutine completes.

blocks.caption: A CPU loop checks its parent cancellation between bounded units of work.

blocks.title: Cancellation boundary
rows: finally; NonCancellable only if suspending and essential

sections.title: CPU and blocking work must cooperate

blocks.text: Most kotlinx.coroutines suspending APIs check cancellation. A CPU loop without suspension must call ensureActive, yield, or another cooperative check. A blocking legacy call may ignore coroutine cancellation until it returns unless the wrapper closes or cancels the underlying resource. Do not add arbitrary yield calls to conceal an unsuitable blocking API. Mutex and atomic operations protect shared state differently, and cleanup must release locks and close resources even on cancellation.

blocks.title: Cancellation is not failure UI
blocks.text: Obsolete structured work should stop quietly unless product semantics say otherwise.

sections.title: Timeout and cleanup boundaries need explicit meaning

blocks.text: withTimeout throws TimeoutCancellationException; withTimeoutOrNull returns null. Place timeouts where the product can define what exceeded its budget: connect, complete request, user operation, or whole workflow. Nested client and coroutine timeouts need documented precedence. Use NonCancellable in finally only for a small suspending cleanup that must complete; it is not a way to continue cancelled business work. Tests should cancel during delay, CPU work, and resource ownership and prove no late state update occurs.

Production readiness requires evidence beyond a happy-path demonstration. State the owner and lifetime of every mutable value, the expected response to failure or cancellation, and the behaviour after recreation or a second simultaneous request. Exercise long and translated content, large font scale, alternate input, slow dependencies, and rapid repeated actions wherever they apply. Prefer deterministic unit tests for pure logic, integration tests at library and protocol boundaries, and device tests when platform lifecycle, rendering, accessibility, or system UI is part of the contract. Do not hide a missing decision behind a generic helper. A future engineer should be able to identify what may run concurrently, what survives, what is authoritative, and which evidence proves the implementation remains correct.

steps.label: Define contract
steps.detail: Name ownership, lifetime, inputs, outputs, failure, and cancellation.

steps.label: Implement
steps.detail: Choose the smallest API that preserves those semantics.

steps.label: Exercise boundaries
steps.detail: Test absence, failure, recreation, concurrency, and unusual input.

steps.label: Collect evidence
steps.detail: Use semantics, deterministic tests, traces, or protocol inspection.

steps.label: Harden
steps.detail: Fix the demonstrated risk and document the remaining trade-off.

blocks.title: Never swallow CancellationException
blocks.text: Converting it to an error lets cancelled work continue and publish stale state.

inspect.title: Preserve cancellation in broad catch
walkthrough: CancellationException is an Exception and can reach this handler.
The code turns normal cancellation into visible error state.
Rethrow cancellation before mapping genuine failures.
inspect.expectedOutput: Replacing or leaving the operation publishes no stale error.

trap_check.mistake: Wrapping an entire workflow in one unexplained timeout.
trap_check.why: The product cannot distinguish connection, server, parsing, or user-operation budgets.
trap_check.fix: Set and name timeouts at boundaries with meaningful recovery.

trap_check.mistake: Adding abstraction or optimisation before defining the failure.
trap_check.why: The code becomes harder while ownership, correctness, or measured cost remains unresolved.
trap_check.fix: First write a boundary test or collect evidence that identifies the real defect.

challenge_intro.task: Implement a cancellable article import with CPU parsing, a closable input resource, an operation timeout, and tests proving no stale publication.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: CPU work checks cancellation. Resources close on success, failure, and cancellation. Timeout and user cancellation have distinct outcomes.

recall.answer: As CancellationException at a cooperative point.
